exercise.name: Commando Pull-up

reference.title: Commando Pull-up
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder adduction and extension, scapular depression, elbow flexion) with a trunk rotation
exercise.laterality: Alternating (head to the right side of the bar, then to the left, in each loop)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull up beside the bar, breathe in on the way down.

prescription.tempo: About 1.3 s up, brief hold, 1.8 s down
prescription.progression: More reps, then a slow lowering, then added weight

cues.text: Stand under the bar so it runs from front to back over your head. Grip it with the hands close together, one in front of the other, palms facing each other; hang with straight arms.
Pull the shoulder blades down first.
Pull up and bring the head past the right side of the bar, turning the chest a little toward it.
Chin above the bar on the right side; the bar sits by the left shoulder.
Lower under control back to the centre hang.
Straight arms, shoulders long, body still.
Pull up again, this time with the head past the left side of the bar.
Chin above the bar on the left side.
Full hang, then repeat to the right.

mistakes.mistake: Hitting the head on the bar
mistakes.fix: Pick the side early and bring the head round the bar, not into it.
Turn from the upper back; keep the legs quiet.
Return to straight arms each rep.

mistakes.mistake: Always going to the same side

mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears.

kinematics.peak: Head to the right: left elbow ≈150°, right ≈84°
kinematics.norm: Nearly straight in the hang to well bent at the top; the arm on the side of the bar bends most (common coaching standard)

kinematics.setup: Neutral, right hand in front, grip points 14 cm apart along the bar
kinematics.norm: Neutral, hands staggered one in front of the other on a bar running front to back (common coaching standard)

kinematics.setup: Head under the bar in the hang
kinematics.peak: Head ≈13 cm to the side of the bar, chest turned 20° toward it
kinematics.norm: The head and trunk move to one side of the bar (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Chin 48 cm below the bar in the hang
kinematics.peak: Chin 2.4 cm (right side) and 2.1 cm (left side) above the bar
kinematics.norm: Chin above the bar, beside it (common coaching standard)

kinematics.peak: About 1.3 s up, 0.4 s hold, 1.8 s down each side
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1.3 s up and 1.8 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Youdas et al. 2010, surface EMG activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise (J Strength Cond Res 24(12):3404-3414)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Check the bar is secure and can take your weight before hanging from it.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Keep the head clear of the bar: move it to the side before the chin reaches bar height.
Step or drop down from the bar with control; do not let go at the top.
modify: Smaller range: go only as high as you can clear the bar.
progressions: Pause with the chin over the bar.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Main mover: pull the upper arms down and back toward the ribs.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Main mover: pull the upper arms down and back toward the ribs.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bend the elbows; the neutral grip shares the work with the brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bend the elbows; the neutral grip shares the work with the brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Pull the shoulder blades down and together as you rise.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Pull the shoulder blades down and together as you rise.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Help pull the arms down and back.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Help pull the arms down and back.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Lower fibres help pull the arms down from overhead.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Lower fibres help pull the arms down from overhead.
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the body hangs in one line without swinging.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the trunk toward the side the head goes, and stop the legs swinging.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Turn the trunk toward the side the head goes, and stop the legs swinging.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Long head helps pull the arm down from overhead.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Long head helps pull the arm down from overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Controls the shoulder blade in the hang.
